# Model zoo

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_model_zoo_docs.py from models/zoo.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every model this project has published a measurement of, with the licence it is offered under, a checksum to confirm you have the same file, and the command that gets it.

## Why this page exists

A result names a model. That name will not obtain the model, will not confirm that the file you obtained is the file that was measured, and says nothing about whether you may redistribute it.

Both gaps were real here. Four published results measure `mobilenetv2-12.onnx`; the file had been deleted from the machine that produced them, nothing recorded where it came from, and all four record `checksum: null`. The measurements outlived the thing measured.

And two published checksums for *byte-identical weights* disagreed. The llama.cpp results hash the weights file; the Ollama results hash Ollama's manifest, which also covers the template and system prompt. One field, two kinds of hash, nothing saying which. That is why every entry below states what its checksum is a hash **of**.

## Licences are read, not assumed

A licence is a legal claim about someone else's work, so each one below records where the claim came from. A licence marked as read from the artifact can be re-derived by anyone holding the file; `aihwbench zoo verify` re-reads it and fails if the manifest and the artifact disagree.

Nothing here is inferred from a model's name, from a sibling model's terms, or from the licence of a repository that happens to host the file. Where a format carries no licence field at all, the entry says the licence was declared by a maintainer and links the terms it was taken from, so you can check it yourself.

**None of this is legal advice, and none of it substitutes for reading the licence.** Verify the terms before you rely on them.

### MobileNet v2 (opset 12)

- **Key**: `mobilenetv2-12`
- **Format**: onnx, 3.5M parameters
- **Size**: 14.0 MB
- **Obtain**: [download](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/onnx/models/main/validated/vision/classification/mobilenet/model/mobilenetv2-12.onnx)
- **Verify**: `aihwbench zoo verify mobilenetv2-12`
- **Licence**: Apache-2.0 — **written by a maintainer.** The format carries no licence field, so nothing re-checks this against the artifact. [Terms](https://github.com/onnx/models/blob/main/LICENSE)
- **Checksum**: `sha256:c0c3f76d93fa3fd6580652a45618618a220fced18babf65774ed169de0432ad5`
  - SHA-256 of the weights file. Identifies the weights and nothing else, so it is the only kind that can be compared across runtimes.

ONNX carries no licence field, so the licence is declared rather than read from the artifact: it is the terms of the ONNX Model Zoo repository that publishes the file. The checksum is of what that URL serves, verified by download. It is deliberately not presented as the identity of the benchmarked file: the four published onnxruntime and openvino results all record checksum: null, so nothing ties them to this or any other file. Results measured after this entry exists can be tied to it; those four cannot, and that is why the entry is here.

## Commands

```bash
aihwbench zoo list              # licences and sources at a glance
aihwbench zoo verify            # check every model this machine can reach
aihwbench zoo fetch <key>       # download, verifying against the checksum
```

`fetch` hashes the bytes as they arrive and deletes a download whose hash does not match, rather than leaving the wrong model on disk where a later benchmark could pick it up.

`verify` reports three outcomes, and the last two are different: the file matches, the file **does not** match, or nothing could be checked. Unchecked is not a pass.
